stories.headline: Carney and Alberta's Smith sign landmark pipeline and carbon pricing deal targeting 2027 construction start
stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith signed an implementation agreement in Calgary on May 15 setting a fall 2027 target for construction approval of a new West Coast bitumen pipeline carrying over one million barrels per day, paired with a revised industrial carbon pricing framework capping Alberta's price at $130 per tonne by 2040 — well below the previously planned $170. The deal drew immediate criticism from environmental groups, B.C., the Bloc Québécois, and the NDP as a 'climate capitulation,' while Poilievre called it insufficient because any carbon price remains. B.C.'s energy minister objected to being excluded from negotiations.

stories.headline: Carney unveils national electricity strategy to double grid capacity by 2050, with expanded role for natural gas
stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney announced Canada's long-awaited National Electricity Strategy on May 14, aiming to double the country's grid capacity by 2050 and lower household energy costs. The plan grants more flexibility to natural gas plants and adjusts clean electricity regulations, drawing criticism that it retreats from the 2030 climate targets. Carney said federal facilitation could also help Quebec and Newfoundland resolve the Churchill Falls hydro dispute.

stories.headline: Alberta separatist petition quashed by court; Carney visits province amid secession controversy

Prime Minister Carney flew to Calgary days later, saying the best place for Alberta is in Canada while also asserting that any independence referendum must comply with the federal Clarity Act and respect Indigenous rights. Premier Smith called the ruling 'anti-democratic.'

stories.headline: New York Times caught using AI-generated fake quote attributed to Poilievre, tightens freelancer AI policy
stories.summary: An April 15 New York Times article about Carney's majority government contained an AI-hallucinated quote attributed to Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre — a fabrication that ran for over two weeks before correction on May 1. The incident, in which the Times' own Canada bureau chief used AI to generate a summary of Poilievre's views presented as a direct quote, prompted the paper to issue a formal warning to freelancers about AI use.

stories.headline: Bank of Canada sees modest AI productivity gains, holds rates amid Iran war and tariff uncertainty
stories.summary: Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Michelle Alexopoulos delivered a widely covered speech on AI's economic impact, finding early signs of modest productivity gains but no evidence yet of widespread job displacement. Separately, minutes from the April 29 rate decision showed the Governing Council felt it could afford to be patient and hold rates steady at 2.25%, while weighing inflation risks from soaring oil prices due to the Iran war against potential economic weakness from U.S. tariffs.

stories.headline: Ontario Liberal nomination dispute over Erskine-Smith's Scarborough Southwest loss triggers party controversy
stories.summary: Federal Liberal MP Nate Erskine-Smith narrowly lost the Ontario Liberal nomination for the Scarborough Southwest provincial byelection to businessman Ahsanul Hafiz, then filed an appeal alleging irregular voting including possible mass membership sign-ups and extra ballots. The Ontario Liberal Party stood by the result. Erskine-Smith subsequently announced he would resign his federal seat this summer and abandon further candidacy, while the controversy was described as an 'unhelpful distraction' for a party trying to rebuild.

Provincial NDP leader Carla Beck declined to meet with Lewis, reflecting tensions over his fossil fuel transition stance versus Saskatchewan's energy realities. Lewis also pushed back on the Carney government's new AI data centres and demanded release of a secret policing deal with China.

stories.headline: Toronto and Montreal compete to host new NATO-aligned Defence, Security and Resilience Bank
stories.summary: Canada was selected to host headquarters for the Defence, Security and Resilience Bank, which will provide long-term financing for defence projects and is expected to bring 3,500 jobs and open by end of 2026. Ontario Premier Doug Ford rallied business leaders for Toronto's bid, while Quebec politicians accused Toronto of waging a 'fear campaign' by invoking the spectre of Quebec separation. Ford disputed this characterization while backing Toronto. Minister Joly, as an MP from Montreal, acknowledged personal bias toward her home city.
